title: data labeling edgecases scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for labeling edge cases and cleanup heuristics for the data-labeling project (customer conversations + product docs). This is informal - notes to self and the start of a guideline doc.

High-level goals:
- Reduce labeler confusion on ambiguous examples.
- Increase inter-annotator agreement (target > 0.82 Kripp alpha).
- Make a short decision tree for common edge cases to include in labeler onboarding.

Notes / principles:
- Prefer conservative labels when intent is unclear: choose 'unknown' / 'requires context' rather than forcing a category.
- When in doubt, add a short rationale comment (1-2 sentences) - valuable for retraining.
- We will later extract patterns from rationales to convert into rules.

Edge cases observed (raw examples + tentative rules):
1) Partial answers / truncated sentences
   - Example: "...and then they just left without saying why." (isolated sentence, no speaker)
   - Rule: If a snippet lacks explicit agent/subject and context, label as 'incomplete' unless preceding/following turns available.

2) Ambiguous pronouns referring out-of-span
   - Example: "He said that would be fine." (who is 'he'?)
   - Rule: If referent is not in the text span, mark 'coref_missing'. Do NOT assume identity from external knowledge.

3) Sarcasm / rhetorical questions
   - Example: "Oh great, another outage - just what we needed."
   - Rule: If clear sarcasm (tone markers, context) then label sentiment opposite of literal. If unclear, mark 'sarcasm_uncertain' and assign neutral.

4) Multiple intents in one snippet
   - Example: "Can you send the invoice and also tell me the ETA?"
   - Rule: Split when possible into two labels (action: 'send_invoice', question: 'ETA_request'). If system requires single label, choose primary intent (first action) and tag multi-intent = true.

5) Sensitive/personal data present
   - Example: "My SSN is 123-45-6789" or phone numbers, credit cards
   - Rule: Label 'sensitive' + redact to allow analytics. Flag for privacy review.

6) Non-English or code-mixed text
   - Example: "¿Cómo estás? I am good, gracias"
   - Rule: If >30% non-English tokens -> label 'non_english'. For short code-mix, label main language and add 'code_mixed' tag.

7) Long multi-sentence context where label depends on previous sentence
   - Rule: Prefer to present annotators with the full conversation window (up to 6 turns). If only single turn available, mark 'insufficient_context'.

Label taxonomy draft (short):
- intent_* (e.g., intent_invoice, intent_ask, intent_cancel)
- sentiment_positive / negative / neutral / sarcasm_uncertain
- status_incomplete / coref_missing / insufficient_context
- sensitive / pii_redact
- language_nonenglish / code_mixed
- misc: multi_intent, requires_followup

Sample labeled examples (for quick copy into training evals):
1) Text: "Please cancel my subscription, I no longer need it."
   Labels: ["intent_cancel", "sentiment_neutral"]
   Rationale: explicit action + clear wording.

2) Text: "I don't think that'll ever work..."
   Labels: ["intent_none", "sentiment_negative"]
   Rationale: opinion, no ask.

3) Text: "He said he'd call back."
   Labels: ["status_incomplete", "coref_missing"]
   Rationale: missing referent.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Thresholds: confirm % non-English token threshold with linguistics (30% is provisional).
- How to represent multi-intent in training: multi-hot vector vs single label + post-processing? Discuss with modeling. (Ping @Liam)
- Build a quick QA test set of 200 of the most ambiguous examples for onboarding. Priority: include sarcasm, coref_missing, truncated.
- Determine whether 'unknown' should be exposed to downstream teams or converted to 'requires_human' in pipeline.

Implementation notes for labeling tool (short):
- Add a free-text 'rationale' field (optional but heavily encouraged).
- Add quick buttons: 'mark_sensitive', 'multi_intent', 'insufficient_context'.
- Show previous 3 turns by default; collapse after first review.

Links / references I keep returning to:
- Confluence: data-labeling-guidelines-draft (CONFLUENCE-7742)
- JIRA ticket for tool changes: JIRA-MLLABEL-198
- PR with sample label schema: github.com/redwood-inference/ml-labeling-pr-42

Notes to self (quick):
- Consolidate this into a 2-page onboarding doc.
- Run a short pilot (N=10 labelers, 500 items) and compute Kripp.
- Add check for PII redaction step before crowd labeling.

Random thoughts / stray lines:
- Might be worth a three-level label: primary intent / secondary intent / contextual flag.
- For sarcasm we could use punctuation heuristics but high FP risk. Better to keep human-in-loop.

-- Asha
